title: Locally quasi-finite morphisms are exactly relative dimension zero
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $x\in X$ let $X_{f(x)}$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})$ its Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] at the point lying over $x$. Then $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] if and only if $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})=0$ for every $x\in X$ (relative dimension zero).

proof.text: For each source point x, quasi-finiteness at x is equivalent to openness of the singleton {f.asFiber x} in the scheme-theoretic fibre. The forward implication is [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated]. For the converse choose affine neighbourhoods U,V with x in U and f(U) contained in V, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] twice. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs] to these opens and use its finite-type and quasi-finite-at-prime witnesses in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. This is the local hpoint equivalence in the Lean proof.

An open singleton has topological Krull dimension at most zero, since its subspace is discrete. It is an open neighbourhood of its point, so [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] gives local dimension at most zero. Every neighbourhood of the point is nonempty and has the irreducible closed subset given by the closure of the point, so its dimension is at least zero. Taking the infimum gives local dimension exactly zero.

Conversely fix x and put Y=X_{f(x)}, y=f.asFiber x. The morphism Y to Spec of the residue field of f(x) is locally of finite type by base change. Its target is locally Noetherian because a field is Noetherian, and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes Y locally Noetherian. Choose an affine open neighbourhood W of y by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Local Noetherianity gives a Noetherian ring of sections on W, and the spectrum homeomorphism makes W a Noetherian topological space (Mathlib noetherianSpace_of_isAffineOpen). By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace], dimension at w=(y in W) is zero.

Unfold the infimum defining local dimension on W. Since its value is zero, it is less than one, so some open neighbourhood V of w has dimension less than one and therefore at most zero. V is Noetherian as a subspace of W and T0 as a scheme subspace. Apply [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite] to the whole closed subset of V, transporting across the homeomorphism between the universal subtype and V. Thus V is finite and every singleton in V is closed. A finite T1 space is discrete, so the singleton of w is open in V. The open inclusions V into W and W into Y carry this singleton to the open singleton {y} in Y.
